DUQUE Secretary to the Sanggunian Municipality of Monkayo Compostela Valley Dear Mr. Duque: This has reference to Resolution bio. 50 of Sangguniang Bayan of Monkayo, Compostela Valley inquiring from this Department on the status of the Indigenous People's (IPs) representation to the local legislative body, in aid of legislation. In this regard, please be informed that we already answered a similar-query in DILG Opinion No. 69, series of 2007, where we opined that RA 8371 and its Implementing Rules issued by the National Commission on indigenous People (NCiP) is already sufficient as an enabling law to install the indigenous peoples representatives in the different Sanggenians of LGUs. Attached herewith is the photocopy of DILG Opinion No. 69 series of 2007 for your ready reference. Thank you. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: JESUS Direc OQU 11 Legai:20/Merle

Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City OIFFIICE OF IFO]IQ LOCAL GOVERINIUIIIÉUIC 69 22 August 2007 DIRECTOR LORETO 1. iBliAGWANU DILG Regional Office No. 09 Zamboanga City Dear Dir. Bhagwani: This refers to your earlier Indorsement of the letter oi Director Celestino D. Talpis, National Commission on indigenous People, Regional Office No. 09, Zamboanga City, endorsing Mr. Timuay Anito L. Tifos as representative of the Indigenous People to the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Zamboanga City, for appropriate action or legal guidance/opinion. In reply thereto, may we first lay down the provisions under RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code, in relation to RA 8371, otherwise known as "The Indigenous People's Rights Act of 1997" with regard to the sectoral representations in all Sanggunians at all levels. To start with, Section 41 (b) and (c) of RA 7160 provides: "(b) The regular members of the sangguniang pan lalawigan, sangguniang pan lungsod, and sangguniang bayan shall be elected by district, as may be provided for by law. Sangguniang barangay members shall be elected at large. The presidents of the leagues of sanggunian members of component cities and municipalities shall serve as ex-officio members of the sangguniang pan lalawigan concerned. The presidents of the liga ng mga barangay and the pederasyon ng rnga sangguniang kabataan elected by their respective chapters, as provided in this Code, shall serve as ex-officio members of the sangguniang and sangguniang pan lungsod, pan lalawigan, sangguniang bayan. In addition thereto, there shall be one (1) (c) sectoral representative from the women, one (I) from the workers, and one (1) from any of the following sectors: the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons, or any other sector as may be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the next local elections, as may be provided for by law. The COMELEC shall promu Igate the rules and reJitlations to effectively

-2- provide for the election representatives. " Of such sectoral With respect to cities, Section 457 of the Local Government Code provides that: "SEC. 457. Composition.- (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, the legislative body of the city, shall be composed of the city vice mayor as presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the city chapter of the liga ng inga barangay, the president of the pantungsod na pedersayon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, and the sectoral representatives, as members. (b) In addition thereto, there shall be three (3) sectoral representatives: one (I) from the women; and, as shall be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the local elections, one (I) from the agricultural or industrial workers; and one (I) from the other sectors, including the urban poor, indigenous cultural minorities, or disabled persons. (c) The regular members of the sangguniang panlungsod and the sectoral repressntatives shall be elected in the manner as mgy be provided for by law. " (underlining ours) Without first dwelling on RA 8371, vvhich is a later law than the Local Government Code, it is clear that under Section 41 (b) of the Local Government Code, the Sanggunian, in addition to the regular and ex-officio members, shall be further composed of 3 sectoral representatives. It is noted that under said provision, the sectors for women and workers are already assured of one seat each. With respect to the other sectors, such as the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons or any other sector, the Sanggunian shall determine within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the next local elections which sector from among the other sectors shall be represented in their respective Sanggunians. Section 41 (b) of the Local Government Code has to be reconciled with Section 457 of the same Code with respect to the composition of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. As to the latter, again, it is provided that in addition to the regular and ex-officio members ot the Sangguniang Panlungsod, there shall be three (3) sectoral representatives in the Sanggunian. What is important to note in Section 457 of the Code is the fact that the women sector is assured of one (1) representation, and that with respect to the workers sector, the Sanggunian is given the option to determine as to whether the sectoral representative for the workers shall come from the agricultural or industrial workers sector. With respect to the third sec!pral representative, again, the Sanggunian is given the power to determine from which sector, including

-3- the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities or disabled persons, shall be represented in the Sanggunian. In this regard, it bears to emphasize further that under the adoresaid Section 457 (c), it is provided that the sectoral representatives of the Sangguniang Panlungsod shall be elected in the manner as may be provided for by law. Unfortunately, however, as of this date, Congress has yet to pass a law providing for [he manner of electing the sectoral representatives in the Sangguniang Paniungsod as mandated under the Local Government Code. This would answer why that even at present, there are still no sectoral representatives in ali the Sanggunians, for thai matter, as provided for by the Local Government Code. Meantime, on 29 October 2007, RA 8371, otherwise known as the "Indigenous People's Rights Act of 1997" was approved and signed into law. Said law recognizes the policy of the State in affording the indigenous people communities adequate representations in the local government Sanggunians at ail levels. Precisely, pursuant to Section 6, Rule IV of the implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 8371, it is mandated that indigenous peoples shall be represented in all Sanggunians at all levels whose representatives shall be selected in accordance with the customs and traditions of uue indigenous people concerned. Along this line, it is noted that it was the National Commission on indigenous People (NCIP), which was mandated by law to come up with the implementing Rules and Regulations. Hence, as in the cases of the provinces of Zamboanga Sibugay and Compostela Valley where the NCIP had already recognized and confirmed the selection of the indigenous people representatives to their respective Sanggunians, this Department also accorded its due recognition based on the confirmation issued by the NC/P. On this note, it bears to emphasize that the assumption of the indigenous peoples representative in the Sanggunian need no other further appointment since their assumption to the local legislative body is mandated by operation of law. The foregoing discussion considered, we are now of the view that Sanggunians of LGUs at all levels shall be composed of its regular members, ex-officio members, the three (3) sectoral representatives per the pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code and one (I) representative from the Indigenous People's Community per RA 8371. With regard to the sectoral representative representing the Indigenous People, clearly, RA 8371 and its Implementing Rules issued by the NCIP is already sufficient as an enabling law to instaii the indigenous peoples representatives in the different Sanggunians of LGUs. Hence, we are of the view that there is no more legal impediment to recognize the assumption of Mr. 'limuay Anito L. Tilos as the official representative of the indigenous people in the Sangguniang Paniungsod of Zamboanga City in view of the recognition and endorsement of NCIP Region 09 Director, Hon. Celestino D. Talp% dated 12 January 2007, that

04 - Mr. Tilos have fully met the requirements provided for by RA 8371 in the selection procedure as iCC/iP representative in the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Zamboanga City. In this regard, may we, however, emphasize that the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Zamboanga City has to enact a City Ordinance providing for the appropriation of city funds for the salaries and other emoluments to be given to the concerned sectoral representative. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A.
